← Back to the journalMATERIAL & CRAFT

Small details. A lasting impression.

Texture, light and a little restraint can transform the way packaging feels.

01

Let the paper set the tone.

A textured paper feels warm and tactile. A smooth wrap gives crisp color and clean print. Start with a paper sample rather than choosing from a screen alone: light, thickness and surface finish change how a color is perceived.

02

Give each finish a purpose.

Foil catches the light. Embossing adds a raised detail. Debossing creates a quieter impression. A single carefully placed finish can be more expressive than several competing treatments. Check fine lines, small type and artwork with the sampling team.

03

Build a coherent set.

Bring the box, insert, tissue, card and shopping bag into the same visual conversation. Repeat a paper, color or ribbon detail across the set, and use a physical prototype to assess the complete experience.
